assessments.reasoning: The pinned Signature Declarations section distinguishes in-subset declarations and extends-type declarations and makes disjointness a trace-wide rule for distinct type branches without an ancestor relationship.

challenge.method: Tested sibling signatures containing the same atom at different states, a parent-child pair, a top-level signature with no extends clause, and overlapping subsets.
challenge.results: The specification rules out the cross-state sibling reuse as well as same-state overlap. An ancestor path permits overlap. A top-level type signature need not spell extends, and subset signatures may overlap.

limitations: The assertion concerns type signatures and the documented Alloy 6 trace scope. It makes no requirement that all type declarations contain an extends token.
